card.name: Tinikling
card.tagline: The Philippines' national dance — dancers leap between bamboo poles clapping at lightning speed.
card.profile: Tinikling (traditionally written tiniclín) is a traditional Philippine folk dance which originated prior to Spanish colonialism in the area. The dance involves at least two people beating, tapping, and sliding bamboo poles on the ground and against each other in coordination with one or more dancers who step over and in between the poles in a dance. It is traditionally danced to rondalla music, a sort of serenade played by an ensemble of stringed instruments which originated in Spain during the Middle Ages. The locomotor movements used in this dance are hopping, jumping, and turning.
card.insight: Tinikling takes its name from the tikling bird — the slender Gallirallus philippensis whose graceful leg movements through rice paddies inspired the choreography; the dance literally translates as 'doing it like the tikling.' Today the Bayanihan Philippine National Folk Dance Company carries Tinikling to global stages, and Filipino schools teach the basics from primary level — a Filipino who can't dance Tinikling is rare anywhere in the world.

parts.note: Tinikling Step Right and Left explanation

steps.name: Tinikling Step Right
steps.description: Hop on left foot outside bamboo, hop on right between poles, hop on left in same spot.

steps.name: Tinikling Step Left
steps.description: Hop on right foot outside bamboo, hop on left between poles, hop on right in same spot.

steps.name: Kuradang Step
steps.description: Change step forward right, step left across right in front.

lessons.teacher_style: The instructor uses detailed voice-over narration with on-screen text descriptions to break down each figure of the dance. They demonstrate the footwork and counts systematically from a front-facing perspective.
lessons.distinctive_method: Combining textbook-style numbered figures with instructional voice-over and on-screen text overlays for traditional Philippine folk dances.
